findings.intrinsic: colsplit (used by GL2RecFromString, GL2Load, GL2LoadLattice, gl2keytab, gl2finetab, gl2labeltab)
findings.description: colsplit := func<s|Split(s,":":IncludeEmpty) cat (s[#s] eq ":" select [""] else [])> compensates for an old Magma behavior in which Split dropped the trailing empty field. In the installed Magma (2.29-8), Split(s,":":IncludeEmpty) already KEEPS all trailing empty fields, so colsplit appends a spurious extra field whenever a line ends with ":". Consequence: GL2RecFromString's assert #colvals eq #icols fails on any serialized record whose last column is empty, which means GL2Save output cannot be re-read by GL2Load whenever the last data column (secs, in the default gl2idatacols) is unassigned in any record — the documented Save/Load and RecToString/RecFromString roundtrips crash. Correct behavior: colsplit(s) must return exactly one field per colon-separated position. Minimal fix for current Magma: drop the compensation. If compatibility with older Magma Split semantics is desired, append the empty field only when Split actually dropped it.

The lookup:=true option of GL2LoadLattice (and hence SL2LoadLattice) always fails with a runtime type error: 'require key: ...' passes the INTEGER column index key to require, which expects a BoolElt, so Magma raises 'Runtime error in require: Logical expected' regardless of whether the key column is present. Should be 'require key gt 0: ...'. Secondary issue on the same code path: line 355 'if lookup then Z:=GL2LookupTable(X); return X,Z; end if;' builds a GL2 lookup table even when sl2 is set (SL2LoadLattice); after fixing the require, the returned table would lack the Z`SL flag and be rejected by SL2LookupLabel ('Lookup table does not contain subgroups of SL2'); it should call SL2LookupTable(X) when sl2 is true.

In the makegroups branch (table entries are tuples <label,group>), the level filter reads r`Level where r is the TUPLE, not the group; tuples have no attributes, so GL2LabelTable(Z : N:=n) with n ne 0 on a lookup table built with makegroups:=true crashes with 'Invalid attribute Level for this object'. Should be r[2]`Level. Identical copy-paste bug in SL2LabelTable at line 469. (N:=0 works because 'N eq 0 or ...' short-circuits.)

findings.intrinsic: gl2keytab / gl2finetab (used by GL2LookupTable, SL2LookupTable with makegroups:=true)
findings.description: With makegroups:=true, the Genus attribute of each constructed group is assigned the STRING Split(l[3],"-")[1] instead of an integer (the attribute is untyped so the assignment silently succeeds). Downstream, GL2Genus(H : NoGenusData) returns H`Genus unchanged, i.e. a MonStgElt like "0" instead of RngIntElt 0; any caller that compares or does arithmetic with the result (e.g. g gt 24 in GL2CPLabels) gets a runtime type error or wrong behavior. Same bug in gl2finetab at line 432. Fix: wrap in atoi(...). (Note the sibling GL2LoadLattice correctly converts genus with atoi at line 348, confirming intent.)

The N and IndexLimit filters parse the label off the first 32 characters of each line via S[i][1..32], which raises 'Sequence indices should be in the range 1 to #S[i]' when a data line is shorter than 32 characters. GL2Load explicitly supports files containing a subset of the gl2rec columns (it maps them via the header), and a legitimate minimal file (label:level:index:negone:gens) can have lines shorter than 32 chars; such a file loads fine without filters but crashes with N or IndexLimit set. Same expression at lines 314 and 320. Fix: clamp the substring to the line length.
findings.proposed_fix:
Current line 310:
            for i:=j to #S do s := Split(S[i][1..32],"."); if atoi(s[1]) eq N and atoi(s[2]) le IndexLimit then
Replacement:
            for i:=j to #S do s := Split(S[i][1..Min(32,#S[i])],"."); if atoi(s[1]) eq N and atoi(s[2]) le IndexLimit then
and the same S[i][1..32] -> S[i][1..Min(32,#S[i])] change at lines 314 and 320.

findings.description: The docstrings of GL2MaxRSZBLabel (line 244) and GL2MaxLMFDBLabel (line 252) say 'Least label in the specified list' but both intrinsics return the LARGEST label (they keep k when Compare(L[i],k) gt 0) — copy-paste from the Min variants. The docstrings should say 'Largest label'.

Docstring claims labels 'of the form N.i.g.n or N.i.g.d.n (N=level, i=index, g=genus, d=determinant index, n=ordinal)' are supported, but the code requires exactly 4 dot-separated components (line 178: require #r eq 4 and #s eq 4) after handling an optional GL1 determinant prefix separated by '-'; a 5-part N.i.g.d.n label raises 'Invalid subgroup label'. The determinant data is actually carried via the 'D-N.i.g.n' prefix form, not a fifth component. The docstring is stale and should describe the D-N.i.g.n form.

Runtime error in 'GL2CompareRSZBLabels': Invalid subgroup label

findings.description: The docstrings of GL2LabelFromRZBLabel (line 1137) and GL2SubgroupFromRZBLabel (line 1143) cite https://doi.org/10.2140/ant.2017.11.1199, which is the Sutherland-Zywina paper; the Rouse-Zureick-Brown label reference is https://doi.org/10.1007/s40993-015-0013-7 (correctly cited in GL2RZBLabel at line 1132). Copy-paste from the SZ intrinsics.
findings.evidence: Reasoning/verified facts: doi 10.2140/ant.2017.11.1199 = Sutherland-Zywina, 'Modular curves of prime-power level with infinitely many rational points', Algebra & Number Theory 11 (2017); doi 10.1007/s40993-015-0013-7 = Rouse & Zureick-Brown, 'Elliptic curves over Q and 2-adic images of Galois', Res. Number Theory (2015). GL2RZBLabel (line 1132) in the same file cites the correct RZB doi; the two inverse intrinsics cite the SZ doi.
findings.proposed_fix: In lines 1137 and 1143 replace 'defined in https://doi.org/10.2140/ant.2017.11.1199' with 'defined in https://doi.org/10.1007/s40993-015-0013-7'.

findings.description: The require error message for an unrecognized Cummins-Pauli label reads 'Invalid Rouse--Zureick-Brown label.' — copy-paste from the RZB intrinsics; it should say 'Invalid Cummins-Pauli label.'

The signature declares '-> MonStgElt' but the intrinsic returns a sequence of label strings (docstring itself says 'List of the Cummins-Pauli labels ... or the empty list'); return type should be SeqEnum. Magma does not enforce declared return types, so this is a documentation/signature error only.
findings.proposed_fix:
Line 1150:
intrinsic GL2CPLabels(H::GrpMat) -> MonStgElt
replace with:
intrinsic GL2CPLabels(H::GrpMat) -> SeqEnum

findings.description: Lines 558-559 (and the parallel 604-605 in SL2LookupLabel) are dead code after 'return NotFound;': 'M := [i:...]; ...; return M[1];'. Besides being unreachable, if ever re-enabled it would return the integer index M[1] rather than the label S[M[1]][1], so it should be deleted or corrected rather than left as a trap.
findings.evidence: Code reading: line 557 'return NotFound;' unconditionally precedes lines 558-559; identical pattern at 603-605. The dead branch also asserts #M eq 1 and returns M[1] (an index), whereas the live loop returns S[i][1] (a label).

findings.description: 'assert IsPrime(2);' is a no-op (2 is always prime); given its position right after the p eq 2 special case and before ChangeRing(H,GF(p)), it is almost certainly a typo for 'assert IsPrime(p);', which would catch non-prime moduli before GF(p) fails with a less clear error. Behavior is otherwise unaffected.
findings.evidence: Code reading: line 862-868 handle p eq 2 and return; line 869 'assert IsPrime(2);' then line 870 ChangeRing(H,GF(p)). GF(p) itself errors for composite p, so the assert as written never fires and never protects anything.

findings.description: Assorted docstring nits found while auditing (no behavior change): (a) line 584 SL2LookupLabel(Z::Tup) docstring says 'subgroup of GL(2,Z/NZ)' — should be SL(2,Z/NZ) (copy-paste from the GL2 version); (b) line 299 GL2Load is declared '-> Assoc, Assoc' and its docstring promises an 'optional' second lookup-table return value, but the body only ever returns X (the only two-value path is the dispatch to GL2LoadLattice, which returns two values only with lookup:=true, and GL2Load never passes lookup); (c) typos: 'basse26' twice in line 183, 'proejction' line 1048, 'idenitied' line 1107, 'Sutherland-Zwyina' line 1118, 'congjugate'/'congjuacy' lines 1152/1161.
findings.evidence: Code reading; for (b): line 327 'return X;' is the only return in GL2Load other than the line 303 dispatch 'return GL2LoadLattice(filename:X:=X,N:=N,IndexLimit:=IndexLimit);' which is called without lookup and therefore also returns a single value.
findings.proposed_fix: Line 584: replace 'The label of the specified subgroup of GL(2,Z/NZ)' with 'The label of the specified subgroup of SL(2,Z/NZ)'. Line 299: either drop the second return type or state that the second value is only returned when the file is a lattice file loaded with lookup. Fix the listed typos in place.

coverage_notes: TESTED empirically (transcripts run against current code): GL2RecToString, GL2RecFromString, GL2CompareRSZBLabels, GL2CompareLMFDBLabels, GL2CoarseLabel (vs LMFDB gps_gl2zhat_fine coarse_label ground truth), GL2SortRSZBLabels, GL2SortLMFDBLabels, GL2SortLabels, GL2Min/Max RSZB/LMFDB Label, GL2Compare/Sort RSZB/LMFDB LabelLists, GL2Save, GL2Load (plain, subset-columns, N/IndexLimit filters, lattice-header dispatch), GL2LoadLattice (plain, N, fineN, IndexLimit, GenusLimit, lookup — lookup is broken, see finding), SL2LoadLattice, gl2keytab/gl2finetab/gl2labeltab via GL2LookupTable (file, Assoc, two-file Tup; with and without makegroups), SL2LookupTable, GL2LabelTable (Assoc N=0/N>0 both branches, file), SL2LabelTable, GL2LookupGroup, SL2LookupGroup, GL2LookupLabel (Assoc + Tup, coarse and fine, conjugated inputs, NotFound), SL2LookupLabel (Assoc), GL2SLabel + GL2SubgroupFromSLabel (30 LMFDB ground-truth pairs at p=5,7,11 PLUS exhaustive roundtrip+injectivity over ALL subgroup conjugacy classes of GL(2,p) for p=2,3,5,7,11,13 — 483 classes total, all pass), GL2SZLabel/GL2LabelFromSZLabel/GL2SubgroupFromSZLabel (17 LMFDB pairs + level/index/genus invariant checks), GL2RZBLabel/GL2LabelFromRZBLabel/GL2SubgroupFromRZBLabel (17 LMFDB pairs incl. fine labels + invariant checks), GL2CPLabels (8 LMFDB pairs) and SL2SubgroupFromCPLabel (9 labels incl. composite levels 6,8,10,12, roundtrip + level/genus). Internal Slabel machinery (MinReps, SplitCartanConjugate, BorelConjugate, NonSplitCartanConjugate, NormalizerSplit/NonSplitCartanConjugate, ConstructA4/S4/A5Subgroup, GroupLabelFromId, GroupIdFromLabel, SubgroupFromLabel, GL2SubgroupID) exercised indirectly but thoroughly by the exhaustive p<=13 roundtrips (covers Borel/Cartan/normalizer/A4/S4/A5 branches; A5 exercised at p=11, the p mod 8 = 5 S4 branch and a=3 A4 branch at p=13). READ ONLY (not directly executed): types(), colindexes and reader/writer function tables (exercised indirectly via Save/Load), the giant szdata/rzbdata/cpdata tables (spot-checked via ~40 LMFDB-verified entries, not exhaustively), cplig (unused anywhere in the package), the dead code after return in the Tup lookup intrinsics. SL2LookupLabel(Z::Tup) fine-group path was not exercised with a genuinely fine SL2 group (setting one up requires an SL2 fine lattice; the coarse path and the analogous GL2 Tup fine path were tested). SL2LookupTable(coarsefile,finefile) untested beyond code reading (identical wrapper to the tested GL2 version). GL2Load's GenusLimit does not exist (only GL2LoadLattice has it) — nothing to test. Assertions excluded from test_code because they hit demonstrated bugs: GL2Save->GL2Load with an empty last column (colsplit bug — worked around by assigning secs), GL2LoadLattice lookup:=true, GL2LabelTable/SL2LabelTable with makegroups+N>0, GL2Load N filter on <32-char lines, GL2Genus integer type on makegroups-table groups; owner should add regression tests for these after fixing.
